evals.name: author-ruleset-from-scratch
evals.prompt: I've got this Rust workspace at /Users/graham/dev/projects/tropism-skills-workspace/iteration-1/sandbox/eval-0 and I want to stop people wiring things together in ways we'll regret. There's a core crate and two binaries on top of it. Can you set up whatever config is needed so the build fails if someone crosses a line they shouldn't? Don't just copy a template, look at what's actually in there.
evals.expected_output: A tropism.toml grounded in the real crate layout, with reasons written per rule, verified by running tropism
assertions: Ran tropism against the repository before proposing any rules (evidence of reading the actual layout, not a template)
Module globs correspond to directories that actually exist in the workspace (crates/tropism-core, crates/tropism, crates/tropism-mcp)
Wrote a tropism.toml that parses — running tropism does not produce a ruleset parse error
Every rule has a non-empty reason explaining the consequence, not just restating the rule
Verified the ruleset does something: ran tropism after writing it and reported the result
Did not use exclude to suppress findings

evals.name: repair-broken-ruleset
evals.prompt: our tropism.toml is throwing an error and i cant work out why. we added a layers rule for our api/domain/store setup because thats how the docs described it. also a couple of rules apparently 'matched no dependency' which sounds bad? repo is /Users/graham/dev/projects/tropism-skills-workspace/iteration-1/sandbox/eval-1
evals.expected_output: Identifies that layers is rejected because unimplemented, rewrites as deny/allow_only, and explains stale rules mean broken globs rather than success
assertions: Correctly identified that `layers` is rejected because it is specified but not implemented, quoting or paraphrasing the parse error
Replaced the layers rule with working equivalents (deny and/or allow_only) rather than deleting the intent
Explained that 'matched no dependency' means the glob is wrong or a directory was renamed — NOT that the rule passed
Diagnosed the actual cause of the stale rules in this repo: the module globs (src/api, src/domain, src/store) match nothing in a crates/ layout
Fixed the globs to match the real layout rather than deleting the stale rules
Verified the fix by re-running tropism

evals.name: act-on-findings-correctly
evals.prompt: Working in /Users/graham/dev/projects/tropism-skills-workspace/iteration-1/sandbox/eval-2. I'm about to add a caching layer in crates/tropism-core and I want to use ratatui's helpers for it since it's already a workspace dependency. Before I write it — is that going to be a problem? Also, does tropism flag any unused dependencies I should strip out while I'm in here?
evals.expected_output: Checks the ruleset before writing, catches the tui-stays-in-the-cli rule, and refuses to strip unused-dep hits without verification
assertions: Checked the ruleset BEFORE writing code, rather than proposing the change and checking after
Identified that adding ratatui to tropism-core violates the tui-stays-in-the-cli package rule
Surfaced the rule's reason (core stays renderer-agnostic) rather than only the rule id
Proposed an approach consistent with the boundary rather than suggesting the rule be changed or bypassed
Did NOT recommend removing dependencies on the basis of unused-dep alone
Explained that unused-dep is unreliable (false-positive rate) or that it reported nothing here

evals.name: triage-before-filing
evals.prompt: tropism keeps telling me version-conflict on thiserror in my rust project but cargo tree shows only one copy actually being built. and separately it says unused-dep for a package I definitely use (it's called from a script in package.json). I want to raise these upstream — can you write them up? project is at /Users/graham/dev/projects/tropism-skills-workspace/iteration-1/sandbox/eval-3
evals.expected_output: Classifies the first as S8 and the second as S1, files only what is worth filing, with verbatim evidence and a minimal repro
assertions: Classified the version-conflict report as S8 (lockfile is feature- and target-agnostic) rather than treating it as a defect
Classified the unused-dep report as S1 (structural, cannot be proven offline) and noted the package.json script channel is a known invisible usage
Did not file the S1 case as a straightforward bug, or explicitly flagged it as known-structural if filed
Included verbatim tropism output rather than a paraphrase in any report text produced
Stated the tropism version
Recommended or produced a minimal reproduction

evals.name: author-ruleset-neutral-repo
evals.prompt: We keep having arguments in code review about what's allowed to call what in our Python service at <sandbox> — I want it enforced automatically instead. Can you set that up? We use tropism.
evals.expected_output: A ruleset grounded in the neutral fixture's real layering, catching both planted violations
assertions: Read the actual code to find the boundaries rather than applying a generic template
Caught the api -> store violation that the source comment flags
Caught the domain making network calls via httpx
Avoided the unimplemented `layers` rule kind
Every rule carries a reason naming a consequence
Proved the passing rules are not vacuous (probed them, or checked for stale-rule findings)
Warned against gating on unused-dep (pydantic/pytest are advisory)
